subject: Delete certification & operational flow — follow-up Q&A

Subject: Delete certification & operational flow — initial questions

Hi Markus / Laura,

Thanks for walking us through the platform demo yesterday. Before legal signs off on the DPA redline we need a bit more color on the operational mechanics for deletion and the certification you reference in section 6.2. Specifically: 

- When a customer requests deletion of a dataset, what are the concrete steps from request -> visible token-level deletion -> backup snapshot purge? Please include estimated timelines for each step (e.g., immediate, 24h, 30d, 90d).
- How do you handle backups/snapshots? Are backups encrypted with separate keys? Are they restored for disaster recovery after a purge request?
- Can you provide a short sample delete certification we can reference in the DPA? We expect an auditable statement with timestamp, scope, and method (logical vs physical).
- In legal hold scenarios, what is the process for holding data and how does that interact with the deletion SLA?

We appreciate a concise operational playbook and a one-page certification template. Tim in procurement is cc'd for procurement/acceptance timing.

Best,
Carolyn
Head of Data Privacy | Acme Corp

From: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Carolyn Jensen <data-privacy@acme-corp.com>, Tim Rhodes <procurement@acme-corp.com>

Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 12:08:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Delete certification & operational flow — initial questions

Carolyn / Tim — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a proposed one-page certification and a short operational playbook (see attachments). High level answers below; happy to walk through on a call.

1) End-to-end timeline (typical flow):
   - Customer delete request received (API/Console): immediate acknowledgement (T0).
   - Logical deletion: we mark tenant objects/dependent records as deleted and remove live-accessible copies from serving layers within 0–2 hours in normal conditions.
   - KV cache + inference cache purge: continuous flushing completes within 2–6 hours depending on workload.
   - Background physical cleanup (tombstone sweep) for primary storage: runs daily; most deletions are fully purged within 30 days.
   - Backup/snapshot purge: retention window is 90 days by default for backups; upon contractual deletion request we can offer an accelerated 30-day backup purge (operational SLA) if elected in the DPA.

2) Backups/snapshots and keys:
   - Backups are encrypted at rest. Production backups use a customer-segregated KMS key for Dedicated/Private customers; hosted customers use per-tenant keys in our KMS.
   - Backups are not routinely restored for single-tenant recoveries after a deletion; restore requires an explicit support/DR action and auditing. After a certified deletion, we will not restore purged data.

3) Certification template (attached): includes deletion timestamp, scope (tenant ID / dataset ID / object prefixes), method (logical purge, tombstone sweep, backup purge scheduling), and operator sign-off.

4) Legal hold interaction:
   - If a lawful hold is in place, we will pause physical purge and backup purge for the specific hold scope and record the hold id + custodian. Holds are visible in the Console and require an authorized legal or security ticket to remove.
   - The DPA must specify hold governance (who can request/remove) and expected maximum hold duration.

Operational note: for customers that require shorter backup purge windows (e.g., 30 days), we need this in the DPA and an on-boarding configuration step; it is a one-time operational commitment.

Next steps: Laura and Karthik — can you confirm the backup purge automation and provide a short, technical addendum we can include in section 6.2 that specifies the job cadence and audit trail locations? I will then send a redline for the DPA reflecting the 30-day accelerated backup purge option and attach the certification template.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-dpa-delete-clause-proposal.docx; flush-playbook-v1.pdf

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 15:42:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Delete certification & operational flow — internal tech notes

Markus / team — quick internal technical confirmation to include in the addendum. Please keep this high-level for the customer docs.

- Primary storage sweep: tombstone sweeper runs nightly at 02:00 UTC; tombstoned blobs are queued for physical deletion; most objects clear the queue within 24–48 hours barring retention holds.
- Backups: we take incremental snapshots every 12 hours and a weekly full snapshot. Backups are retained in our object store under lifecycle rules; a backup purge request triggers a flagged lifecycle transition and a final delete job within the configured window (30/90 days).
- Key handling: for Dedicated we rotate keys quarterly; for hosted customers keys are per-tenant and can be BYOK for customers requiring on-prem HSM; we record key version used to encrypt each backup and include that in the certification.
- Audit trail: delete operation events, operator IDs, and job run ids are written to the Compliance Logs bucket and are available via Console for 365 days (longer retention available as an add-on).

Recommend we add the following two short sentences to 6.2 (operational appendix):
"Delete requests are acknowledged immediately. Physical purge of primary storage is executed by nightly sweep jobs; backup lifecycle transitions are scheduled per the agreed retention window and are auditable via Compliance Logs"

If that looks good, Mina — can you produce the exact log keys/paths where the evidence will be stored so we can point Carolyn to the exact locations in the addendum?

-karthik
Senior Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks for the rapid responses and the attachments — that helps a lot. A few clarifying follow-ups after we reviewed the playbook: 

- Acme is aligned with the proposed 0–2h logical purge and nightly tombstone sweep. We would like the DPA to include an explicit maximum time-to-physical-purge for primary storage ("physical purge completed within 30 days except for lawful hold"), and to add the 30-day backup purge option as an exhibit.
- Regarding backups: can you confirm that backup encryption key versions used for the copies that are purged will be referenced in the certification? That is a requirement for our internal audit.
- Legal hold: we need the DPA to require Redwood to provide hold metadata (requester, ticket id, scope, start timestamp) within 24 hours of hold creation. Is that operationally feasible?

If you can confirm the three points in writing we should be able to accept the proposed language and sign the DPA; procurement is ready to proceed once the exhibit is attached. 

Carolyn
Head of Data Privacy | Acme Corp
